work_order.understanding:
The plan reviewer refused the previous revision on one point and was right, and I reproduced the objection rather than conceding it. AC-15 stated the rule 'so each case fails when the guard it covers is removed' and then prescribed unwrapping the parseNote call in validateFile back to the bare matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8')) as the falsification. I ran exactly that against the previous revision's fix: the gate still exits 1, still prints exactly one ::error:: line and still writes 0 bytes to stderr, because the top-level boundary catches the YAMLException and emits '::error::Release notes check failed: missed comma between flow collection entries...'. The only thing that changes is that the line stops naming the file. No case in the six-case suite asserted on that, so the suite stayed green. The criterion claimed coverage the suite did not have, and its own verification procedure, followed literally, would have reported success on a suite that does not test the call site at all.

I take the reviewer's option (a), not (b). I checked the alternative empirically rather than assuming: the assertion that makes the case falsifiable is 'the ::error:: line contains broken.md', which returns 0 matches with the guard unwrapped and 1 match with it in place. Option (b) would have deleted the clause instead, and the deleted clause is the only mechanism standing between this bug class and its third recurrence. So this revision is additive: a seventh test case that spawns bin/release-notes-check.mjs with BASE_REF=base against a sandbox holding `category: [unclosed`, asserting exit 1, at least one line starting ::error::, zero bytes on stderr, and that some ::error:: line contains 'broken.md'. It reuses the git setup the sixth case already builds, so the cost is one more spawn in a sandbox the suite already constructs. AC-15 is rewritten to name the two spawn cases explicitly and to drop the unverifiable clause. Everything else from the refused revision stands unchanged.

The previous revision's diagnosis was NOT wrong, and I want to be precise about that, because the two are easy to confuse. It correctly identified that the original plan's failure was applying 'report rather than throw' per call site rather than as a boundary, and it found the third instance (EISDIR inside reportError itself) that per-call-site work structurally cannot reach. I re-verified all four defects at the PR commit before proposing anything: BUG-1(a), BUG-1(b), BUG-2 and the EISDIR case all reproduce with 0 ::error:: lines on stdout. What was wrong was only the test design, and the reviewer's proposed fix is a correction to the tests, not a redirection of the work.

One correction to the previous revision's own claims, since it is mine and QA will read the new criteria against it. It stated the 8000-note branch produces 1728000 bytes of diff output; I measured 1808000 with the same recipe. That does not change anything - both are over the 1MB ceiling by the same order of magnitude and the fix raises it 64x - but the qa_script now carries the number I actually measured rather than the inherited one.
work_order.root_cause: The gate's pipeline has no error boundary, and its reporting function is not itself total. Every throw escapes the `void (async () => { ... })()` IIFE as an unhandled rejection and terminates Node with a stack trace on stderr and zero `::error::` lines on stdout - for a gate whose entire job is to write an annotation. The PR applied its guard per call site, so each guard left its immediate neighbours exposed; the third instance proves the shape cannot converge, because it lives inside reportError itself, downstream of every guard added. Separately and differently fixable: promisify(execFile) applies a 1MB maxBuffer to `git diff`, which is a ceiling on legitimate branch size rather than a failure at all.
work_order.approach:
Put one boundary under the pipeline, and move the three shapes of failure into small total functions that vitest can finally reach. This is deliberately NOT QA's suggested one-liner and NOT a re-run of the original plan's approach. The previous revision's design stands; the change here is the seventh test case that answers the reviewer.

NEW FILE `packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/failures.mjs`, three exported functions, each total over one failure shape:
  1. `describeFailure(error)` - returns ONE line, never a stack. Recognise an `execFile` rejection by its own `cmd`/`code`/`stderr` properties and render `git <subcommand> failed with exit <code>: <git stderr flattened to one line>`; that names the failing command and the offending revision, which a raw `Command failed: git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR ...` dump does not. Fall back to `error.message`, then `error.name`, then `String(error)` for a non-Error throw, so it cannot itself throw. Verified shape: `git diff failed with exit 128: fatal: bad revision 'origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD'`.
  2. `readReadme(readmePath)` - returns the file's text or `''`, catching EVERY throw. This subsumes the existing `fs.existsSync` pre-check, so that double lookup goes away rather than being wrapped twice.
  3. `parseNote(path)` - returns `{ ok: true, data, content }` or `{ ok: false, message }`, wrapping BOTH `readFileSync` and `matter()`. This is where BUG-2 is caught, and it is caught HERE rather than only at the boundary so the message can name the note: `Release note <label> could not be parsed: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 3, column 1`. I verified this matters: with the boundary in place but parseNote removed, BUG-2 produces `Release notes check failed: missed comma between flow collection entries...` - exit 1, no stack, but nothing telling the contributor which file is theirs. The boundary alone is a regression detector here; parseNote is what makes the message usable. That difference is also exactly what makes the new seventh test case falsifiable.

Put them in `src/` beside `util.mjs`, which `bin/release-notes-check.mjs` already imports from. That is what makes them testable at all - `src/**/*.test.*` is vitest's include, so this is the only way the file under repair acquires coverage without restructuring the gate.

EDIT `packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs`, six edits:
  (a) import the three helpers.
  (b) `reportError` calls `readReadme` in place of its inline `existsSync`/`readFileSync` pair. `reportError` becomes total, so the EISDIR case reports instead of crashing.
  (c) `validateFile` calls `parseNote`; on `!ok` it calls `reportError` with the label and the parse message and returns false. All SEVEN of its existing reportError messages keep their exact current text - only the parse gains a guard. Grep for them; do not trust a count.
  (d) DROP `import matter from 'gray-matter';` from the bin script. After (c) it has no remaining reference, and `.oxlintrc.json` sets `no-unused-vars: error`, so leaving it fails `yarn lint`. `fs` stays - it is still used by `createWriteStream` and `existsSync`.
  (e) Rename the IIFE to `async function main() { ... }` and end the file with `void main().catch(e => reportError(`Release notes check failed: ${describeFailure(e)}`));`. This is the boundary. It covers the `git diff` call (BUG-1a), the maxBuffer residue, and anything a future edit adds.
  (f) KEEP the per-call `try/catch` around `git fetch` exactly as PR #32 has it. Removing it would be a re-roll; it is correct, it produces the message QA has already verified against AC-10, and the boundary sits under it without changing it. I re-verified AC-10's message is byte-identical after the patch. Add `{ maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 }` alongside the existing `{ encoding: 'latin1' }` on the diff call, with a comment saying why: ~64x Node's 1MB default and ~35x the 1808000 bytes I measured, so no human branch reaches it, and if one ever did the boundary reports it as an annotation rather than a stack.

NEW FILE `packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/failures.test.js`, SEVEN cases. Five unit cases against the real filesystem via `fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir())` - no stubbing, so the EISDIR case is a genuine reproduction rather than a mock agreeing with itself: a thrown execFile rejection renders one line naming the command; `describeFailure` handles a plain Error and a non-Error throw; a README that is a directory yields `''`; a note with `category: [unclosed` yields `ok: false` carrying the YAML reason; a well-formed note passes through unchanged, so the catch cannot silently swallow a valid note.

Two are spawn cases, and both are the answer to the reviewer's objection.

The sixth spawns the real `bin/release-notes-check.mjs` with `child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [scriptPath], { cwd: sandbox, env: { ...process.env, BASE_REF: 'qa-tag-1', GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: undefined }, encoding: 'utf-8' })` and asserts exit 1, at least one line starting `::error::`, and zero bytes on stderr. It fails if `void main().catch(...)` is removed.

The seventh is new and is what makes AC-15 true. It spawns the same script with `BASE_REF: 'base'` against a sandbox whose branch commits a note with front matter `category: [unclosed`, and asserts FOUR things, not three: exit 1, at least one line starting `::error::`, zero bytes on stderr, AND that some `::error::` line contains the string `broken.md`. That last clause is the load-bearing one and it is the correction the reviewer asked for. I ran both directions against the real script: with the parseNote call site in place the error line contains `broken.md` (1 match); with it unwrapped back to `matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8'))` and the boundary intact, the run still exits 1 with one `::error::` line and 0 stderr bytes - so the first three assertions pass unchanged - but the line reads `Release notes check failed: missed comma...` and contains `broken.md` zero times. The fourth assertion is therefore the one that fails, and the case is genuinely falsifiable where the previous revision's six-case suite was not.

Both spawn cases share one sandbox builder: `fs.mkdtempSync` a directory, `git init --bare` a remote, clone it, seed `upcoming-release-notes/README.md` plus a valid note on a `base` branch, push it, branch, commit, and `git tag qa-tag-1 && git push origin qa-tag-1`. Set GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in the spawn env - CI has no global git identity and the commit fails without them. Derive scriptPath from `import.meta.url` (`new URL('../../bin/release-notes-check.mjs', import.meta.url)`) so it does not depend on the runner's cwd. I built and ran this exact setup by hand against the extracted PR script and against the patched copy, in both directions, and it works with no global git identity configured. Do NOT skip the git setup on grounds of speed - it is a handful of local commands and it is the only thing in the suite that exercises the boundary or the call site.

Put the new tests in a NEW file rather than extending `util.test.js` on purpose: AC-7 asserts `util.test.js reports 33 passing`, and keeping them separate means that criterion stays literally true rather than being quietly rewritten.

Plus one release note.

I applied all of the above to a copy of the PR's script and ran every case against a real bare-remote sandbox. Results: BUG-1(a) `::error::Release notes check failed: git diff failed with exit 128: fatal: bad revision 'origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD'`, exit 1, stderr 0 bytes; the 1808000-byte diff `Validated 8000 release note(s)`, exit 0; BUG-2 `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/broken.md could not be parsed: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 3, column 1`, exit 1, stderr 0 bytes; the EISDIR case exit 1, 1 `::error::`, 1 `::notice::` (empty), stderr 0 bytes; a valid note still exits 0 with `Validated 1 release note(s)`; AC-10's message unchanged; and all five AC-8 regression branches byte-identical in stdout and exit code to the unmodified PR-32 script.

files.change: Three exported total functions: `describeFailure(error)` returning one line for an ::error:: annotation (recognising an execFile rejection by its cmd/code/stderr and naming the git subcommand and exit code, falling back to error.message/error.name then String(error)); `readReadme(readmePath)` returning the file's text or '' on any throw; `parseNote(path)` returning { ok: true, data, content } or { ok: false, message }, wrapping both readFileSync and matter(). Module doc comment recording the invariant that none of the three may throw, since each sits on the failure path.
files.why: Put the failure handling in src/, which vitest covers, instead of bin/, which nothing covers. This is what turns 'wrap two more call sites' into a boundary that CI can hold in place.

files.change: Import the three helpers. Drop the now-unused `import matter from 'gray-matter'` (no-unused-vars is an error in .oxlintrc.json, so leaving it fails lint; `fs` is still needed for createWriteStream and existsSync). reportError uses readReadme in place of its inline existsSync/readFileSync pair, making the error reporter total. validateFile calls parseNote and, on !ok, calls reportError with `Release note <label> could not be parsed: <message>` and returns false, leaving its seven existing messages byte-identical. Rename the `void (async () => {...})()` to `async function main()` and terminate the file with `void main().catch(e => reportError(`Release notes check failed: ${describeFailure(e)}`));`. Add `maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024` to the git diff call's existing options object, with a comment saying it is a deliberate widening over Node's 1MB default (~35x the 1808000 bytes measured) and that the boundary catches the residue. KEEP the existing per-call try/catch around `git fetch` exactly as it stands.
files.why: Holds BUG-1 (both triggers) and BUG-2, and closes the EISDIR instance inside reportError. Retaining the fetch guard is deliberate: it is already verified by AC-10 and replacing it would discard passing work.

files.change: Seven cases. Five unit cases under a temp directory made with fs.mkdtempSync: describeFailure on an execFile rejection naming the command; describeFailure on a plain Error and on a non-Error throw; readReadme on a path that is a directory returning ''; parseNote on front matter `category: [unclosed` returning ok: false with the YAML reason; parseNote on a well-formed note returning ok: true with its data, so the new catch cannot swallow a valid release note. Plus TWO spawn cases against the real bin/release-notes-check.mjs, sharing one sandbox builder that makes a fs.mkdtempSync dir with a bare remote, a `base` branch and a pushed tag `qa-tag-1`, GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in the env and scriptPath derived from import.meta.url. The first runs BASE_REF=qa-tag-1 and asserts exit 1, an ::error:: line, and 0 bytes on stderr. The second, which is the reviewer's correction, runs BASE_REF=base against a branch committing a note with front matter `category: [unclosed` and asserts exit 1, an ::error:: line, 0 bytes on stderr, AND that some ::error:: line contains 'broken.md' — the last assertion is what fails when the parseNote call site is unwrapped, and I verified both directions by hand.
files.why: The gate in bin/ has no coverage today, which is why its perimeter rotted unnoticed. Two spawn cases, not one: the six-case suite the reviewer read could not distinguish 'the parseNote guard is present' from 'the parseNote guard is removed', because the boundary alone already produced exit 1, one ::error:: line and empty stderr. The seventh case's filename assertion is what closes that.

files.change: Release note, category Bugfix, authors [Shivam-Fl], single-line body stating that the check reports a bad base ref, unreadable README or malformed note front matter as an annotation instead of a Node stack trace, and validates branches whose release-note diff is large. No slug collision with fix-release-notes-gate-crashes.md or fix-release-notes-gate-io-paths.md.

acceptance.how_to_verify: This is the permanence mechanism, and the previous revision of this criterion claimed coverage its suite did not have — the reviewer's objection, which I reproduced. It is now true, and this is the check that establishes it. Run the suite and confirm all seven cases in failures.test.js execute. Then falsify each guard in turn, and hold the criterion to its own stated rule. (1) Remove `void main().catch(...)`: the tag-ref spawn case must fail — I measured 0 ::error:: lines and 6 stderr frames without it, against 1 ::error:: line and 0 stderr frames with it. Restore it. (2) Unwrap the parseNote call in validateFile back to the bare `matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8'))` the PR had, keeping the boundary: the malformed-front-matter spawn case must fail ON THE FILENAME ASSERTION specifically. A run that stays green after deleting the guards proves nothing; a run that goes green on the first three assertions of case 7 and is only stopped by its fourth proves the case is real.

AC-15: run the package suite and confirm all seven cases in failures.test.js execute. Then prove falsifiability in both directions, and check each against what the suite actually does. Delete `void main().catch(...)` and confirm the tag-ref spawn case fails. Restore, unwrap the parseNote call back to `matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8'))`, and confirm the malformed-note spawn case fails — and confirm it fails on the assertion that the ::error:: line contains 'broken.md', not on exit code or stderr length, which will both stay correct in that direction. If either spawn case is skipped or the git setup is short-circuited, say so — the criterion is void without it.
Finally: `yarn lint` and `yarn typecheck` from the repo root (lint will catch a leftover `import matter` in the bin script), and confirm the new release note passes the gate this change touched.
risks: Adding the boundary means a programming error inside the gate now reads as 'Release notes check failed: ...' rather than as a crash. That is the deliberate trade this whole ticket asks for — the same one reportError already made for its reads — but it means a future bug in the gate can be mistaken for a contributor's mistake. The message carries the real error text, which is what makes that recoverable; do not also dump a stack to stderr, because several criteria check stderr is empty.

parseNote now returns a tagged result rather than throwing, so validateFile's first lines change shape. Every one of its seven reportError messages must keep its exact current text or AC-8's byte-for-byte comparison fails. Grep for them rather than trusting the count.

The 64MB maxBuffer is a magic number with a comment. A pathological diff now costs up to 64MB of resident buffer before it errors, which is a deliberate exchange: an error that names itself is cheaper than a process that dies.

The two spawned-gate cases run real git. They create a bare remote and commit under a tmpdir on every suite run — fast, but they are the first tests in this package to shell out, so they can fail on a machine with no git identity or an unusual git default branch name. Set GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in the env and pass explicit branch names, and do not assert on `master` vs `main`.

Moving failure handling into src/ adds a file under a path the release-notes generator and packages/docs/scripts also consume. Confirm neither imports a name from failures.mjs by accident, and that nothing in those consumers starts resolving a new module.

Keeping the git fetch guard while adding the boundary leaves two nested handlers for one failure class. That is intentional and AC-10's verified message depends on the inner one winning, but a future reader may 'clean up' the inner guard and silently change AC-10's output.
out_of_scope: Making the gate WORK on a tag-shaped BASE_REF rather than merely reporting it — resolving the merge base with `git merge-base` or fetching into an explicit ref instead of assuming `origin/<ref>` exists. QA flagged that it could not confirm how a tag-shaped ref reaches the gate, and I found the producer: .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml sets BASE_REF to `github.event.pull_request.base.ref`, which is a branch name, so the tag trigger is not reachable through that action as written. That lowers the urgency of BUG-1(a) but does not change the contract, and the file is under `.github/**`, which no ticket may change. Recorded rather than folded in.
PR #30's missing [AI] title prefix: a merged PR and repository metadata, no file to edit. A human runs `gh pr edit 30 --title '[AI] ...'`. Carried forward unchanged from the previous order.
selectReleaseNotePaths, SELECTED_STATUSES and the --diff-filter=AMR invocation: verified correct in both directions and pre-blessed in AC-8. The C-row fixture stays exactly as PR #32 left it.
parseReleaseNotes and formatNotes in util.mjs: used by release-notes-generate.mjs and packages/docs/scripts, they never decode a diff, so neither the latin1 view nor this change reaches them.

The pre-existing process.exit(1) at the top of the file for an unset BASE_REF: its message is a fixed 85 bytes and it runs before anything is pending, so it cannot be truncated and cannot lose its exit code. Left alone as before.
A general restructure of the gate into a single testable runCheck() under src/. It would give the same coverage with a larger diff against ten criteria that currently pass byte-for-byte.

Handling EPIPE on process.stdout. It is the one remaining way the gate can die without an ::error:: line, but it is a stream failure rather than a call failure and no criterion covers it; recorded in residual_risks instead.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Every defect in this order was reproduced by me at the PR-32 commit d1cbb0f against a real bare-remote git sandbox, running the actual bin/release-notes-check.mjs extracted from that commit. BUG-1(a) (a BASE_REF that fetches but will not resolve as origin/<ref>): stdout 0 bytes, 0 ::error:: lines, stderr a 6-frame Error ending 'fatal: bad revision', exit 1, with `git fetch origin qa-tag-1` exiting 0 first so the failure is provably the diff and not the fetch. BUG-1(b): a branch of 8000 notes with 200-byte filenames gives 1808000 bytes of `git diff --name-status -z` output; the gate then emits stdout 0 bytes and RangeError [ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER] on stderr. BUG-2 (front matter `category: [unclosed`): stdout 0 bytes and a 10-frame YAMLException. The third instance, which QA did not report: replacing README.md with a directory prints 1 ::error:: line, 0 ::notice:: lines, then dies on a 5-frame EISDIR raised inside reportError itself. I then applied this order's whole fix to a copy of that script and re-ran all four plus the regressions: BUG-1(a) becomes '::error::Release notes check failed: git diff failed with exit 128: fatal: bad revision origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD', exit 1, stderr 0 bytes; BUG-1(b) becomes 'Validated 8000 release note(s)', exit 0, stderr 0 bytes; BUG-2 becomes '::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/broken.md could not be parsed: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 3, column 1', exit 1, stderr 0 bytes; the EISDIR case becomes 1 ::error:: plus 1 ::notice::, exit 1, stderr 0 bytes. All five AC-8 regression branches produce stdout and exit codes byte-identical to the unmodified PR-32 script, and AC-10's message is unchanged. I also ran the reviewer's objection to ground rather than argue it: with the boundary present and the parseNote call site unwrapped back to bare matter(fs.readFileSync(...)), the spawned gate still exits 1 with one ::error:: line and 0 bytes on stderr, so the previous revision's suite genuinely would not have noticed - and the assertion 'that line contains broken.md' does notice (0 matches unwrapped, 1 match restored). Held at 90 rather than higher by three things I could not run here: this checkout has no node_modules, so I could not execute the new failures.test.js through vitest, nor run yarn typecheck or yarn lint; I ran on Node 22.23.3 while the invoking action pins Node 24; and the spawn-based cases were validated by running the identical spawnSync calls by hand against the extracted script rather than through the test runner.
evidence: BUG-1(a) at the PR-32 commit d1cbb0f, reproduced in a bare-remote sandbox by running the extracted script: BASE_REF=qa-tag-1 -> stdout 0 bytes, 0 lines starting ::error::, stderr 'Error: Command failed: git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/' with 'fatal: bad revision', 6 stack frames, exit 1. Run side by side: `git fetch origin qa-tag-1` exits 0 and `git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD` exits 128, so the failure is provably the diff and not the fetch.

BUG-1(b) at the same commit: a branch with 8000 notes and 200-byte filenames, `git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/ | wc -c` = 1808000. Running the gate gives stdout 0 bytes, 0 ::error:: lines, stderr 'RangeError [ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER]: stdout maxBuffer length exceeded', exit 1 — matching QA's H-12.

BUG-2 at the same commit: front matter `category: [unclosed` gives stdout 0 bytes, 0 ::error:: lines, stderr a 10-frame 'YAMLException: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 3, column 1' ending in 'Node.js v22.23.3', exit 1 — matching QA's H-9 frame for frame.

Third instance, found while reproducing the first two and not in QA's report: on a branch where upcoming-release-notes/README.md is replaced by a directory, reportError's own fs.readFileSync throws EISDIR. The run prints 1 ::error:: line and 0 ::notice:: lines (140 bytes of stdout), then dies on a raw 'Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read' stack with 5 frames, the first application frame being reportError itself.

Fix verified in the same sandbox against a patched copy of the PR's script: BUG-1(a) -> '::error::Release notes check failed: git diff failed with exit 128: fatal: bad revision origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD', exit 1, stderr 0 bytes. BUG-1(b) -> 'Validated 8000 release note(s). 🎉', exit 0, stderr 0 bytes. BUG-2 -> '::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/broken.md could not be parsed: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 3, column 1', exit 1, stderr 0 bytes. EISDIR case -> exit 1, 1 ::error::, 1 ::notice:: (empty), stderr 0 bytes. A valid note still exits 0 with 'Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉'.

AC-8 regression, measured: five sandbox branches (valid note; `category: Nonsense`; git mv seed.md seed2.md; no note added; README deleted plus a Nonsense note) run against both the unmodified PR-32 script and the patched one, with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set. cmp reports the stdout files equal and the exit-code files equal on all five (0/1/1/1/1). AC-10's message is byte-identical too: '::error::Could not fetch base ref "nonexistent-branch" from origin: Command failed: git fetch origin nonexistent-branch...' with 0 bytes on stderr.

The reviewer's objection, reproduced rather than conceded. Spawning the patched gate with BASE_REF=base against a sandbox whose branch commits front matter `category: [unclosed`: with the parseNote call site in place, exit 1, 1 ::error:: line, 0 bytes stderr, and the line contains 'broken.md' (1 match). With that call site unwrapped back to `matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8'))` and the top-level boundary intact, the run STILL exits 1 with 1 ::error:: line and 0 bytes stderr — so the first three assertions pass unchanged — but the line reads '::error::Release notes check failed: missed comma between flow collection entries...' and contains 'broken.md' 0 times. Restoring the call site returns the match to 1. This is what the seventh case asserts and it is why the sixth-case suite the reviewer read could not falsify that guard.

Source confirming the coverage gap: packages/ci-actions/vitest.config.mts has include: ['src/**/*.test.(js|jsx|ts|tsx)'], while the gate is packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs — so nothing in CI exercised the file under repair.

alternatives_considered.approach: The reviewer's option (b): keep the refused revision's six cases and rewrite AC-15's how_to_verify and qa_script step to falsify only what the suite can falsify, stating plainly that the validateFile call site is held by AC-13's hand-run rather than by CI.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the criterion honest by giving up the mechanism. AC-15 is the only thing that stops a third recurrence of this bug class, and the defect it lets through is precisely the one QA's BUG-2 is: with the boundary alone, the gate tells a contributor their YAML is broken without telling them which of their files is. I verified option (a) costs one extra spawn in a sandbox the suite already builds, so there is no real trade-off to weigh — deleting the clause buys nothing that adding the assertion does not also buy.

alternatives_considered.approach: QA's hint: widen the existing try to cover both git calls, a one-line change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It treats the symptom QA happened to observe. It leaves matter() throwing (BUG-2) and leaves reportError's own read throwing (the EISDIR instance I reproduced), and it establishes no boundary for whatever a future edit adds — which is the failure mode that produced this loop in the first place. It also cannot fix BUG-1(b) properly: catching a too-large diff reports an error for a branch that ought to pass, whereas raising maxBuffer makes it validate. I measured both outcomes.

alternatives_considered.approach: A top-level .catch on the async IIFE and nothing else — the change the original plan considered and rejected.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The boundary itself is right and it is the core of this plan too, but alone it leaves the three failure shapes untested and it inherits a useless message: a bare catch emits 'Command failed: git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/qa-tag-1...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/', a 160-character command echo that names neither the subcommand nor the revision. I also measured, this time directly, the second half of that: a bare catch turns BUG-2 into 'Release notes check failed: missed comma between flow collection entries...' — clean, no stack, and useless to the contributor who has to guess which note is broken. Rejecting it originally was the error; adopting it unaccompanied would repeat that error one level down.

alternatives_considered.approach: Restructure the whole gate into a single exported runCheck() under src/, so the entire pipeline is unit-testable at once.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It gives the same coverage behind a much larger diff against ten acceptance criteria that currently pass byte-for-byte. Extracting the three failure shapes plus two spawned end-to-end cases gives the boundary a name, a message and a test each, at a fraction of the churn — and leaves the ordinary verdicts, which AC-8 compares byte for byte, untouched. I confirmed this by running the five AC-8 branches against the patched script and getting identical output.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the tag case by resolving the merge base properly (git merge-base, or fetching into an explicit FETCH_HEAD) so BASE_REF=qa-tag-1 works instead of erroring.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes which branches pass the gate, and I found the producer of BASE_REF: .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml passes `github.event.pull_request.base.ref`, a branch name, so the tag case is not reachable through the vendored action — and that file is under `.github/**`, which no ticket may change. It would also not touch BUG-1(b) or BUG-2 at all.

assumptions: The ten acceptance criteria that passed on PR #32 still describe the intended behaviour, and this change must leave every one of them byte-identical. I verified AC-8's full five-branch comparison against a patched copy (all identical on stdout and exit code), AC-10's message, and the valid-note path; the rest are left to the implementer and QA.
Vitest's include stays src/**/*.test.*. A bin/*.test.mjs harness would have to change vitest.config.mts; putting the logic in src/ avoids that.
util.test.js must keep reporting exactly 33 tests, because AC-7 states that number. Hence new tests go in a new file rather than extending util.test.js.

The two spawned-gate cases can create a bare remote and commit inside a tmpdir in the CI environment. I ran the identical spawnSync against the extracted script by hand, in both falsification directions, and it worked with no global git identity configured provided GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* are set in the env — which is why the tests set them.
CI runs Node 24; I reproduced and verified everything on Node 22.23.3, which is what this checkout has. The invoking action pins node-version 24.

The bare-remote sandbox reproduces how Actions populates BASE_REF, on QA's own record that BASE_REF=base resolves identically there and on the vendored action.yml that sets it from the pull request's base ref.
unknowns: Whether any consumer outside this repository depends on the exact wording of the gate's messages. AC-10 and AC-13 pin two of them, but I cannot grep for external consumers.

Whether Node 24's execFile maxBuffer behaviour differs from Node 22's in a way that moves the ceiling. The fix raises the ceiling rather than relying on where it sits, so this only affects the comment's arithmetic.
Whether diff sizes between normal and 1808000 bytes degrade anywhere before the ceiling. I measured the over-the-line case and normal cases only.

Whether the spawn-based tests' git setup is reliable on every CI runner (Windows in particular, where the tmpdir and shell quoting differ). The package's suite otherwise runs pure Node with no git, so these are the first such dependency in it.

Whether the reviewer will accept a seventh case as the answer or wants the criterion narrowed anyway. I chose the option that makes the criterion's own stated rule true rather than the one that makes the criterion stop claiming it, and I have reproduced the objection against the previous suite so the choice is evidenced rather than argued.
residual_risks: EPIPE is still unhandled. If the gate's stdout is closed early (`node release-notes-check.mjs | head -1`), console.log raises EPIPE asynchronously as an unhandled 'error' event on process.stdout, and a top-level .catch cannot see it. This is the one remaining way the gate can die without an ::error:: line, and it needs a `process.stdout.on('error', ...)` to close. I did not fold it in because it is a different failure shape (a stream, not a call) and no criterion covers it.

The boundary catches errors; it does not verify them. A diff that resolves but lists a path the gate then mis-parses still produces whatever selectReleaseNotePaths returns, and the boundary says nothing about correctness there.

BUG-1(a)'s tag trigger is not reachable through the vendored action as written, so AC-11 is verified against a constructed case. Its production frequency is unmeasured and may be zero — the criterion is retained anyway because the boundary it verifies is what every other failure depends on.

The seven new tests prove the failure paths report rather than crash. They do not prove the gate's verdicts are still correct on ordinary branches; AC-8 remains the only check for that, and it is a hand-run comparison.

The seventh case's falsifiability depends on the ::error:: line containing the filename, which in turn depends on parseNote producing a label that reaches reportError. If a future edit changes how validateFile labels its paths, the assertion still holds or fails on its merits rather than silently passing — but it is an assertion on a message string, so it is coupled to that wording.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs:140`

Evidence: Built a sandbox with a real bare remote (git init --bare base, clone, push base and sdlc/issue-31), installed real gray-matter + listify, and ran the PR's script. With BASE_REF set to a tag, `git fetch origin v9.9.9` SUCCEEDS (tags are fetchable), so the new catch at line 133 never fires, and line 140 dies:

  $ BASE_REF=v9.9.9 GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rv/t.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs
  exit=1
  node:internal/errors:983
  Error: Command failed: git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/v9.9.9...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/
  fatal: bad revision 'origin/v9.9.9...HEAD'

Same result on origin/main's script, so this is not a regression — it is the same defect class the PR set out to close, left at the sibling call site. A second reachable trigger, in a `git clone --depth 1 --no-single-branch` checkout (the actions/checkout default): `git fetch origin base` succeeds and creates `origin/base`, but the three-dot diff then fails with `fatal: origin/base...HEAD: no merge base`, again uncaught:

  shallow_file=yes
  -- origin/base after fetch -- 37b81b3...  EXISTS
  Error: Command failed: git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD ...
  fatal: origin/base...HEAD: no merge base

Reachability is limited today: BASE_REF comes from github.event.pull_request.base.ref (always a branch), and .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml is not referenced by any workflow (grep -rn 'release-notes/check' .github/workflows/ returns no match). But the fix is one line, and the ticket's own root_cause names 'of a reachable base ref' as one of the three unguarded assumptions.

Fix: Extend the existing try block at line 132 to cover the `git diff` as well, routing its failure to `reportError` with the same contract as the fetch — e.g. move the `git diff` call inside the `try`, or wrap it in its own catch that calls reportError(...) and returns. A base ref that is unfetchable and one that is unfetchable-as-a-revision then both produce a ::error:: line and exit 1.

qa.title: The git diff call is left unguarded, so two git failures still crash the gate with a raw stack trace
qa.expected: Every way the two git calls can fail produces a ::error:: line and exit 1, which is the contract the PR states for the fetch: "This function's contract is to report rather than throw, so the same treatment the file reads get applies here."
qa.actual: The try/catch wraps only `git fetch`. The `git diff` on the next statement still rejects into an async IIFE with no catch. Two triggers confirmed: (a) a BASE_REF that fetches but does not resolve as origin/<ref> — a tag is enough — which yields 'fatal: bad revision' and a 6-frame Error stack; (b) diff output over execFile's 1MB default maxBuffer — 1768000 bytes was enough — which yields RangeError [ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER]. In both, stdout carries zero ::error:: lines. The exit code is 1, but only because Node terminates on the unhandled rejection.
qa.suspected_cause: The guard was applied per-call-site rather than to the git invocation as a whole. Both execFile calls sit in the same function and can reject for the same environmental reasons, so the narrow fix the work order considered — wrapping the one fetch — leaves its immediate neighbour unguarded. Widening the existing try to cover both calls is a one-line change and is still narrower than the top-level .catch the work order rejected.

qa.title: A release note with malformed YAML front matter crashes the gate instead of reporting it
qa.expected: A note the gate cannot parse is reported the way every other invalid note is — a ::error:: naming the file and what is wrong with it — and the run exits 1.
qa.actual: matter(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf-8')) in validateFile is not wrapped, so a YAMLException escapes into the async IIFE. stdout is empty: zero ::error:: lines. stderr is a 10-frame YAMLException stack ending 'Node.js v22.23.3'. Exit 1 via the uncaught throw. The contributor who made the typo gets a Node stack trace in the job log instead of the annotation telling them their front matter is malformed.
qa.suspected_cause: validateFile assumes gray-matter always parses. Every other validation failure in the function is funnelled through reportError; the parse is the one step that can throw, and it sits outside that funnel. This is the same 'report, do not throw' contract the PR restores for I/O, applied to content parsing.
